NutriForge Foods - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriForge Foods Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if using a telephone, or click the Q&A button in the webcast interface if online. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Vice President of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriForge Foods' Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Growth Officer; and Morgan Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on eight key areas: EPS guidance and key assumptions, revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance, volume and price/mix analysis, performance in key channels including retail, foodservice, and convenience, impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, organic revenue growth overall and by region, discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, and progress on sustainability initiatives and goals.

First, regarding EPS guidance and key assumptions: As we close out a solid quarter with adjusted EPS of $1.28, up 12% from last year, we're guiding full-year adjusted diluted EPS to $4.50 to $4.70, implying 8% to 13% growth at the midpoint versus 2023's $4.18. This excludes further M&A beyond our EcoSip acquisition and assumes stable FX. Revenue growth factors in 5% to 6% organic at midpoint, with 3 to 4 points from pricing and 2 from volumes and mix. In core beverages, we're looking at flat to 1% volume in carbonated soft drinks, balanced by strength in functional lines like ZeroNutri, where non-CSDs now make up 45% of our mix, up from 38%, with energy and hydration up 15%. Health and wellness should see 10% to 12% organic growth, led by innovations like OatFlex capturing quick market share similar to category disruptors. Internationally, North America at 6%, APAC tempered to 4% on China softness, EMEA at 9% via sponsorships, and LatAm at 7% with hedges on inputs. Gross margins expand 110 to 130 basis points to 42.5% on 1% to 2% input deflation—aluminum down 5%, sugar easing—plus $150 million in productivity from AI demand tools and robotics. SG&A down 40 bps, op margins up 50 bps. Balance sheet solid with $2.8 billion cash, $1 billion buyback program. Risks include inflation at 2.5% to 3%, no recession, FX neutral; we're well-hedged.

Second, concerning revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance: Building on Q3 strength, we're raising the midpoint across metrics. Net revenue now 5% to 7% reported, 4% to 6% organic, including bolt-ons like BioFresh. Op profit margins up 100 to 150 bps to 16.0% to 16.4%, EPS $5.75 to $5.95 or 12% to 16% growth, FCF $6.8 to $7.2 billion. Beverages 5% to 7% organic with margin expansion, snacks 4% to 6%, nutrition 6% to 8%. North America 5% to 7%, Europe 3% to 5%, emerging 7% to 9%. This reflects premiumization, $1.8 billion savings, hedging below spot on cocoa and dairy.

Third, in terms of volume and price/mix analysis: Organic growth of 4.8% broke into 2.7% volume and 2.1% price/mix. Volumes up across beverages at 3.2% on non-carb surge like HydroBoost gaining 1.2 share points, snacks 2.4% on savory strength, health 6.8%. Regionally strong in North America 3.1%, APAC 4.5%. Price/mix moderated but solid at 2.1%, with net pricing 2.8% offset by mix shifts. Premiums now 28% of mix. Enablers include AI inventory cutting stockouts 22%.

Fourth, looking at performance in key channels: retail, foodservice, convenience: Channels grew 7.2% organic. Retail at 58% of sales up 8.6% on premium mix, ForgeFit snacks up 14%, e-comm 22%. Foodservice 6.8% on QSR recovery, new contracts with Yum. Convenience 9.4% fastest, energy multipacks 16% at c-stores, APAC 13.7%.

Fifth, reviewing impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue: FX was an 8-point headwind to reported growth, turning 6.8% organic into 1.2% reported. Euro down 12% hit Europe 2.5 points, LatAm currencies volatile 3 points despite 12% organic, APAC 2.5 points. Cumulative 12-month drag $450 million. Hedged 75% of 2024 revenue, localizing sourcing to 85%.

Sixth, analyzing organic revenue growth: overall and by region: Global organic 7.8%, with 4.2% pricing, 2.1% volume, 1.5% mix. North America 9.2% on RTD coffee, Europe 6.4% on plant-based, APAC 8.1%, LatAm 4.9%. Innovations like Hydrate+ up 25%.

Seventh, examining discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies: Pricing averaged 5.6%, passing 62% of 9.1% input inflation. Beverages 4.2%, snacks 6.8%, dairy 7.1%. Regional: NA 5.9%, APAC/LatAm 6.7%. RGM via AI elasticity models, premium to 42%, promo optimization down to 18.2%, 14 new products.

Eighth, considering progress on sustainability initiatives and goals: Scope 1/2 emissions down 28%, 65% renewables. 92% priority commodities responsibly sourced, 88% deforestation-free. Packaging 35% to 100% recyclable goal, water intensity down 19%. Savings $112 million, boosting margins 80 bps.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Lee (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $12.8 billion, representing a 7% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 42.5%, bolstered by commodity cost deflation and productivity gains. Operating income was $2.8 billion, and earnings per share were $1.28. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $2.8 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases, with $400 million executed year-to-date under our $1 billion authorization.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for adjusted diluted EPS of $4.50 to $4.70, alongside the raised revenue and margin outlooks Alex detailed.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, thank you. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

Mike Johnson (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Good question, Mike. Inflation remains a factor, but we've navigated it effectively through targeted pricing up 5.6% on average, covering 62% of the 9.1% input cost rise in areas like cocoa up sharply earlier. Elasticity is holding better than industry averages—around -1.4 in health products—allowing volume resilience. Our hedging at 85% on key agri inputs like sugar and wheat, plus productivity from AI and dual-sourcing, has kept gross margins expanding. We're passing costs thoughtfully by category, with stronger execution in snacks and emerging markets where demand stays inelastic.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Lisa Chen (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for OatFlex, our new plant-based RTD, and what is the expected impact?

Taylor Kim (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Lisa. OatFlex, our almond-oat blend RTD, is off to a hot start, grabbing 8% U.S. plant-milk share in three months post-launch, much like explosive entries in the space. Plans include expanding to 15,000 more doors in convenience and club channels next quarter, plus APAC rollout via e-comm partners. Expected impact: 10% to 12% growth contribution to health segment, driving overall organic top-line by 1 point in FY24, with 15% margins from premium positioning and supply efficiencies.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

David Patel (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Morgan Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
David, we've built resilience through dual-sourcing from regions like India and Vietnam, hedging 80% on commodities like cocoa and sugar, and AI-driven demand sensing via SAP integrations cutting waste 15% and stockouts 22%. Capacity adds at Monterrey and Zhengzhou plants give 15% headroom. For disruptions like potential avian flu or port issues, our Zero Waste program recycles 95% PET, and Route Optimization 2.0 saves $120 million annually. This de-risks us versus 2023 shortages in juice or dairy.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Emma Rodriguez with Bank of America. Please proceed.

Emma Rodriguez (Bank of America):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Jordan Lee (CFO):
Emma, Q4 organic growth should hit 4% to 5%, with volumes 2.5% to 3% and price/mix 1.5% to 2%. Full-year on track with raised guidance, assuming CPI 2.5% to 3%, stable FX, no recession. Upside from premium shifts and input easing; we're hedged on risks like El Niño or strikes. Long-term, mid-teens EPS growth via our premium, purposeful strategy outperforming peers.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriForge Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
